Boston arrives as the better team at five on five, holding 54% of the expected goals in its games to Anaheim's 46%. The Ducks create slightly more per 60 minutes (3.08 expected goals for, against 2.97 for BOS) but give up more (3.27 against, to 2.93), which is the gap that matters. The model sees a close game, projecting BOS for 3.05 goals and ANA for 2.64.

Special teams tilt toward Anaheim's power play, which generates 0.64 expected goals a game against Boston's 0.43. Both penalty kills allow about the same (0.66 for BOS, 0.64 for ANA). Boston takes 4.7 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents chances, though Anaheim draws just 4.2. In net, projected starter Jeremy Swayman is at a .930 save percentage and +4.93 goals saved above expected this season, on top of +26.52 across 55 games last year. Projected Anaheim starter Lukas Dostal sits at .892 and +1.07 this year, after -3.71 over 56 games last season.

Both clubs are 3-2-0 in their last five with 50% of the expected goals, and both played on October 13, so rest is even at two days. Boston's recent wins came by 6-1, 5-1 and 6-3, though it was outplayed in the 6-1 game (34% of the chances). For tonight, the model likes Pavel Zacha (29%) and David Pastrnak (28%) to score for Boston, with Pastrnak at 27% for two or more points. For Anaheim, Beckett Sennecke and Cutter Gauthier are each at 29% to score, and Leo Carlsson is at 26% for a multi-point night.
